title: Fast weights (2016)
matchup: Ba, Hinton, Mnih, Leibo and Ionescu (2016) vs Schmidhuber (1991, 1992, 1993)
question: Do Schmidhuber's 1991-93 fast weight programmers establish the priority he claims for the mechanism and recursion described by Ba and colleagues in 2016?

usual_credit.summary: Jimmy Ba and colleagues' 2016 paper adds a decaying matrix of fast weights to a recurrent network, storing outer products of recent hidden states and interpreting the result as attention to the recent past. Its implementation includes layer normalization and an inner settling loop, and it credits earlier fast-weight ideas by Hinton and Plaut and Schmidhuber. The 2021 Turing Lecture later cites this work for high-capacity short-term memory. The disputed credit concerns which parts of that mechanism and motivation were already present in the 1991-93 work, rather than the first use of any fast-changing weight.

works.who: Jimmy Ba, Geoffrey Hinton, Volodymyr Mnih, Joel Z. Leibo, Catalin Ionescu
works.title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
Using fast weights to deblur old memories

claim.summary: Schmidhuber argues that his 1991-92 fast weight controllers already trained a slow network to program another network's changing weights, and that his 1993 paper extended the idea to a recurrent network programming its own fast weights. He regards Ba and colleagues' outer-product memory and its high-capacity motivation as substantially the same approach. He also challenges the 2016 statement that the earlier papers did not implement the specified form of recursion, pointing to experiments in the 1991 report. His complaint includes the later Turing Lecture's attribution to the 2016 paper, while acknowledging still earlier fast-weight proposals.

quotes.text: A quarter century later, others followed this approach.
Hinton's 2016 paper[FWP4a] did not make clear that much of it was a rehash of my papers on fast weight programmers
ignoring my even earlier papers[FWP0-1] which did describe experiments with such an implementation
As recently as of 2022, Hinton[HIN22] asks: "For sequential data, is it possible to use fast weights to mimic a simplified Transformer?"
This motivation and a variant of the method was republished over two decades later.

response.summary: Ba and colleagues cite Schmidhuber's 1993 paper and credit it with explaining end-to-end backpropagation for such a system. They distinguish their implemented recursion and attention interpretation from the earlier proposals, while crediting Hinton and Plaut's 1987 suggestion. Their method adds decay, normalization and a settling loop to the fast memory. Irie and Gershman's 2025 primer describes it as a special instantiation of recurrent fast weight programmers; Irie has co-authored work with Schmidhuber. These sources acknowledge a relationship but do not provide a direct answer from the 2016 authors to his later complaint about priority or earlier experiments.

quotes.text: Schmidhuber [1993] pointed out that a system of this kind could be trained end-to-end using backpropagation
but neither of these papers actually implemented this method of achieving recursion.

agreed_facts: Schmidhuber's report FKI-147-91 is dated 26 March 1991 and the journal version appeared in Neural Computation 4(1) in 1992, and the report's two experiments are a flip-flop task with unknown time delays and a temporary variable binding task: https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/FKI-147-91ocr.pdf

Schmidhuber's 1993 ICANN paper (pages 460-463) includes the weights of a fully recurrent network among the time-varying variables that can store temporal information, and changes them with an update that adds a product of unit activations passed through differentiable thresholding functions: https://sferics.idsia.ch/pub/juergen/ratio.pdf

Ba et al. posted their paper to arXiv on 20 October 2016 and published it at NIPS 2016, and its references include Hinton and Plaut (1987), Schmidhuber (1993) and Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997) but no other work by Schmidhuber: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.06258 https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2016/hash/9f44e956e3a2b7b5598c625fcc802c36-Abstract.html

Both the 2016 paper and the 1993 paper update a weight matrix during a sequence by adding products of unit activations and train the slow weights by gradient descent. The 2016 paper adds exponential decay (0.95 in its experiments), layer normalization and an inner loop of settling steps, and it shows that the fast weight matrix is equivalent to attending to earlier hidden states: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.06258

The 2021 Turing lecture cites Ba et al. (2016) for the statement that fast weights create a high-capacity, short-term memory, and Schmidhuber's Turing-award page gives the year of that paper as 2014 while his priority-disputes page gives 2016: https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~hinton/absps/ACM21.pdf https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/scientific-integrity-turing-award-deep-learning.html https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/ai-priority-disputes.html#hintonfast
Hinton's 2022 Forward-Forward paper asks whether fast weights can be used to mimic a simplified Transformer and cites Ba et al. (2016) for the question: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.13345
crux: The dispute is whether the 2016 recurrent network with decaying outer-product fast weights is a republication of Schmidhuber's 1993 recurrent fast weight programmer and its 1991-92 feed-forward precursors, or a separate proposal that builds on Hinton and Plaut's 1987 idea and adds decay, layer normalization and an interpretation as attention. A narrower question concerns the 2016 sentence saying that neither Hinton and Plaut nor the 1993 paper actually implemented the method of achieving recursion. Schmidhuber points to the experiments of his 1991 report, which are a flip-flop task with unknown time delays and a temporary variable binding task, and the question is whether those count as implementing what the 2016 sentence describes.

card.headline: Fast weights
card.question: Is the 2016 fast-weights method new, or a version of his 1991-93 work?
card.claim: He says his 1991-93 papers already trained one network to rewrite another's weights, then its own, and that the 2016 paper largely rehashed them.
card.pushback: Ba and colleagues cite his 1993 paper but say it did not implement this recursion, and they add decay, normalization and an attention interpretation.
card.crux: The question is whether decay, normalization and an attention interpretation make the 2016 method new or a repeat of the 1993 design.
